Shape sensing endoscope fiber: I thought it is sensing shape of the target at the end of the fiber, but it is actually sensing the shape of the fiber itself.
It's made with a few twisted fibers with bragg grating, which let's you measure local strains and thus curvatures.

Fig. 1-2: Lamb2024, Shape sensing endoscope fiber
https://doi.org/10.1364/OPTICA.532250
Fig. 3-4: Paloschi2020, 3D Shape Sensing With Multicore Optical Fibers: Transformation Matrices Versus Frenet-Serret Equations for Real-Time Application
https://doi.org/10.1109/JSEN.2020.3032480

The spectrum and the wavelength shift of the bragg grating looks pretty clean. They could measure curvature as small as 2.6 mm, and relative error of the shape with ~ 1%. For large curvature it gets less accurate because of smaller strain. (Bronnikov2019
https://doi.org/10.1364/OE.380816)

ofc this would have application in robotics esp. soft robotics. This paper built a soft bending actuator with a fiber optic shape sensor (FOSS) in its body. It works so well they could sweep the actuator tip over different shaped surfaces, and reconstruct the shapes.

Our couch was God's footstool, and we were sheltered from the dews of heaven by the forest foliage. We were lulled to sleep by the croaking of the frog, the chirping of the cricket, the whooping of the owl and the yell of the panther! distributed Raman amplifications are so nice, no need for specialized fibers, no need for repeaters/OEO conversions, no additional delays. Just a mux for you to launch the pump, which is a shorter wavelength laser shifted by the Raman phonon freq, and you can even pump more wavelengths to get broader gain bw.
however, it is weak in fibers, and you need tens of km of fibers for decent gain. So to make it small and relevant in shorter reach scenarios, you start looking for stronger Raman with tighter confinement, and suddenly all the other nonlinearities start to bite you, two-photon absorptions, four wave mixing.. and you start yearning for diamond based PIC because it has such good bulk properties, but most of the diamond PIC demos are for quantum stuff (translation: low power and low bandwidth).
photonics folks are still stuck with no single do-almost-everything material like Si and SiO2 did for cmos (at least initially), and instead have to play with a dozen different materials most of which have near zero volume. One for the lasers & amplifiers, one for the modulators, one for the detectors, and one for low-loss routings. Especially amplifiers, such a primitive component, and you still cannot ask for a few nice things at the same time.

by the way these, these are some of the best amplifiers, and the C band people have grinded them out at volume. Maybe O band is just cursed because praseodymium hates silica.
